sense: good and decent, of a person or an act

evidence: Cic. Amic. 44: ut ab amīcīs honesta petāmus
Cic. Fin. 4.25: nec honestō quicquam honestius (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “honorable, respectable, creditable, worthy, virtuous, decent, proper”. As a noun, honestum is moral goodness, the philosophers’ word for the right. Its first sense is respected, of good standing.
Of persons, upright and honest; of things and craftsmen, good of their kind, excellent (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Plaut. Capt. 5.2.6: sī eris vērāx, tuā ex rē faciēs (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: haec igitur prīma lēx amīcitiae sanciātur, ut ab amīcīs honesta petāmus, amīcōrum causā honesta faciāmus
phrases.english: let this, then, be laid down as the first law of friendship: that we ask of friends only what is right, and do only what is right for their sake

phrases.latin: breve enim tempus aetātis satis longum est ad bene honestēque vīvendum
phrases.english: for a short span of life is long enough to live well and honourably

phrases.latin: probum patrem esse oportet, quī gnātum suom esse probiōrem quam ipsus fuerit postulat
phrases.english: a father who demands that his son be better than he was himself ought to be a good man
